newsitem.title: USA: U.S. high-grade corporate issuance may hit $1 bln.
newsitem.headline: U.S. high-grade corporate issuance may hit $1 bln.

text.p: Another $1.0 billion-plus day of fresh supply may be in store for U.S. corporate bond investors on Wednesday, led by a $600 million 30-year offering from Chrysler Corp, syndicate sources said.

A multi-market sell-off after inflation warnings from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan was not expected to hinder either the Chrysler deal or a planned $250 million 10-year note offering from Smith Barney Holdings Inc, said officials not included in those syndicates.
Salomon Brothers, lead manager for Chrysler's deal, did not immediately return phone calls.

The Chrysler deal is expected to consist of an A3/A-minus rated 30-year debt priced at 68 to 69 basis points over Treasuries. The deal will include an unusual make-whole call at Treasuries plus 18 basis points, one source said.
Smith Barney Holdings' $250 million offering, coming on the heels of a successful $750 million offering from Salomon Bros on Tuesday, could come at a tight 60 basis point spread.

If anything, Greenspan's comments on Wednesday may cause markets to pause, a syndicate official said. But because of longstanding powerful demand for higher yielding paper, any back-up in yield should actually be welcomed, he said.

"Demand has been really good and there will be more demand with obviously higher rates," said a syndicate chief at a big New York firm. "The two year at six percent is a magical number when you're buying. Then you could have issuers being a little cautious on the long end."
In his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony, Greenspan warned that financial markets, including stock and junk bond prices, may be overly optimistic about the economy, and urged caution.
Also on Wednesday, Seagate Technology Inc is expected to issue a three-part Baa3/BBB rated $750 million debt offering via Morgan Stanley & Co, sources said.
